title: Trinetra
subtitle: त्रिनेत्र · the three-eyed
body_markdown:
His right eye is the sun, his left the moon, and the third is fire. Two eyes see the world; the third sees through it. When it opens, whatever is false turns to ash.

This is the guru bead, where the count begins and ends. On a mala you never cross it; you turn back and begin again.

title: Lingodbhava
subtitle: लिङ्गोद्भव · the pillar without end
body_markdown:
Brahma and Vishnu argued over who was greater. A pillar of fire split the dark between them. Vishnu, as a boar, dug down; Brahma, as a swan, flew up. Neither found an end. Shiva stepped out of the flame.

*The infinite cannot be measured, only bowed to. Remembered on Mahashivaratri.*

title: Adiyogi
subtitle: आदियोगी · the first yogi
body_markdown:
In yogic lore, a figure sat in the Himalayas so still that most who came drifted away. Seven stayed. After years of waiting, on the first full moon after the summer solstice, he turned south and began to teach. They became the Saptarishis.

*The first guru. That full moon is Guru Purnima.*

title: Neelakantha
subtitle: नीलकण्ठ · the blue-throated
body_markdown:
Gods and demons churned the ocean for nectar. First came Halahala, a poison that could end every world. Shiva drank it. Parvati pressed his throat so it went no further, and it stayed there, blue.

*He takes in what no one else can bear.*

title: Chandrashekhara
subtitle: चन्द्रशेखर · the moon-crowned
body_markdown:
The Moon married Daksha's twenty-seven daughters, the Nakshatras, but loved only Rohini. Daksha cursed him to waste away. The dying Moon prayed at Somnath, and Shiva set him on his head, where he still wanes and returns.

*Refuge for the fading, not only the worthy.*

title: Virabhadra
subtitle: वीरभद्र · born of wrath
body_markdown:
Daksha held a great sacrifice and shunned Shiva. Sati, Shiva's wife and Daksha's daughter, gave up her body in its fire. Shiva tore out a lock of hair and struck the earth. Virabhadra rose from it and razed the sacrifice.

*Grief, turned into force.*

title: Kamantaka
subtitle: कामान्तक · the ender of desire
body_markdown:
Only a son of Shiva could kill the demon Taraka, but Shiva sat lost in tapas. The gods sent Kama to stir him. Kama's flower-arrow struck, and the third eye opened. Kama fell as ash.

*Desire lives on without a body, as Ananga. What the third eye burns is illusion.*

title: Kalyanasundara
subtitle: कल्याणसुन्दर · the beautiful bridegroom
body_markdown:
Parvati sought Shiva through years of fierce tapas. He came disguised as an old ascetic and mocked Shiva to test her; she would not hear it. They married in the Himalayas, with Vishnu giving the bride away and Brahma as priest.

*Love, won by steadiness.*

title: Ardhanarishvara
subtitle: अर्धनारीश्वर · the lord who is half woman
body_markdown:
The sage Bhringi would circle only Shiva, never Parvati. He even became a bee to squeeze between them. So Parvati merged into Shiva's left side, making one body.

*Shiva and Shakti, still and moving, cannot be worshipped apart.*

title: Somaskanda
subtitle: सोमास्कन्द · with Uma and Skanda
body_markdown:
Shiva's seed burned too hot to hold. Agni carried it and the Ganga cooled it until it came to rest in a bed of reeds. Six babies were born there, nursed by the six Krittikas. Parvati embraced them into one six-faced child, Kartikeya, who killed Taraka.

*The family: father, mother, son.*

title: Gangadhara
subtitle: गङ्गाधर · bearer of the Ganga
body_markdown:
King Bhagiratha called the heavenly Ganga down to free his ancestors' souls. Her fall would have shattered the earth. Shiva caught her in his matted locks and let her out as a gentle stream.

*Power is made kind by what receives it.*

title: Dakshinamurti
subtitle: दक्षिणामूर्ति · the south-facing teacher
body_markdown:
Under a banyan, a young teacher faces south. Before him sit aged sages. He does not speak, yet their doubts dissolve.

*The highest teaching is given in silence. His fingers form the chin mudra: the self joined to the absolute.*

title: Bhairava
subtitle: भैरव · the terrible
body_markdown:
Brahma, then five-headed, boasted that he was supreme. Bhairava sprang from Shiva's anger and nipped off the fifth head. The skull clung to his hand, and he wandered as a beggar until it fell away in Kashi.

*Pride is cut, and even Shiva's form bears the cost. Bhairava now guards Kashi.*

title: Vishvanatha
subtitle: विश्वनाथ · lord of the universe
body_markdown:
Kashi rests on the tip of Shiva's trident, so even the great dissolution cannot touch it. It is said that to anyone who dies there, Shiva whispers the mantra that ends rebirth.

*In Kashi, death is a doorway. Its fires at Manikarnika never go out.*

title: Bhikshatana
subtitle: भिक्षाटन · the wandering beggar
body_markdown:
Shiva walked into the pine forest as a naked, radiant beggar. The sages' wives followed him. The furious sages sent a tiger, a serpent and a demon dwarf against him. He wore the tiger's skin, the serpent as an ornament, and danced on the dwarf.

*Ritual without humility, humbled.*

title: Tripurantaka
subtitle: त्रिपुरान्तक · destroyer of the three cities
body_markdown:
Three demons ruled three flying cities of gold, silver and iron. Only a single arrow, loosed when all three lined up, could end them. The earth became Shiva's chariot, Mount Meru his bow and Vishnu his arrow. One shot, and all three burned.

*Celebrated as Dev Deepavali.*

title: Gajantaka
subtitle: गजान्तक · slayer of the elephant
body_markdown:
The elephant demon Gajasura attacked devotees in Kashi. Shiva burst out of the linga and killed him. The dying demon asked for one thing: that Shiva wear his hide. He did.

*Even a foe, surrendered, is carried. Hence Krittivasa: clothed in hide.*

title: Andhakantaka
subtitle: अन्धकान्तक · ender of Andhaka
body_markdown:
Parvati playfully covered Shiva's eyes, and the world went dark. From that darkness a blind child was born, Andhaka. He grew into a demon who desired Parvati herself. Shiva impaled him on the trident. Every drop of his blood spawned another Andhaka, until the goddesses drank it all.

*Darkness born of closed eyes.*

title: Jalandharari
subtitle: जलन्धरारि · foe of Jalandhara
body_markdown:
Fire from the third eye, cast into the ocean, became the demon Jalandhara. His wife Vrinda's devotion made him invincible. When he came for Parvati, Vishnu broke that shield by deceit. Shiva drew a disc in the water with his toe and ended him.

*Vrinda's curse on Vishnu is why the tulsi plant is holy.*

title: Kalantaka
subtitle: कालान्तक · the ender of death
body_markdown:
Markandeya was fated to die at sixteen. When Yama came, the boy clung to a linga, and Yama's noose looped around both. Shiva burst out and kicked Death away.

*Markandeya stays sixteen forever. Remembered in the Mahamrityunjaya mantra.*

title: Kiratamurti
subtitle: किरातमूर्ति · the hunter
body_markdown:
Arjuna did tapas for a divine weapon. A boar charged him, and he and a wild hunter shot it at the same moment. They fought over the kill, and Arjuna lost. Then he saw his offering to Shiva garlanding the hunter's neck. Shiva revealed himself and gave him the Pashupata.

*The god tests before he gives.*

title: Ravananugraha
subtitle: रावणानुग्रह · grace to Ravana
body_markdown:
Ravana tried to lift Mount Kailash. Shiva pressed down with one toe, and the mountain pinned his arms. Crying out, Ravana sang Shiva's praise for ages. Shiva freed him and named him Ravana, 'the one who roared'.

*Tradition credits him with the Shiva Tandava Stotram.*

title: Vaidyanatha
subtitle: वैद्यनाथ · lord of physicians
body_markdown:
Ravana cut off his heads one by one as offerings, and Shiva healed each like a physician. Granted a linga for Lanka, he was told never to set it down. The gods tricked him into handing it to a cowherd, who set it down at Deoghar. It stays there still.

*Healer, even of the proud.*

title: Bholenath
subtitle: भोलेनाथ · the innocent lord
body_markdown:
Shiva granted Bhasmasura a boon: whatever he touched on the head would turn to ash. Bhasmasura came to try it on Shiva. Vishnu appeared as the dancer Mohini, and the demon copied her dance until his hand touched his own head.

*Shiva gives freely, even unwisely.*

title: Harihara
subtitle: हरिहर · half Vishnu, half Shiva
body_markdown:
Devotees argued over whether Vishnu or Shiva was greater. At Sankarankovil, the goddess prayed to see the answer. Shiva appeared as one body: dark Vishnu on one side, pale Shiva on the other.

*The quarrel was only in the watchers.*

title: Kalahastishvara
subtitle: कालहस्तीश्वर · lord at Kalahasti
body_markdown:
The hunter Kannappa worshipped a linga with meat and water carried in his mouth. One day the linga's eye bled, so he gouged out his own and set it there. When the other eye bled, he put his foot on the spot to guide his hand and reached for his last eye. Shiva caught his hand.

*Love without ritual.*

title: Kedareshwara
subtitle: केदारेश्वर · lord of Kedar
body_markdown:
After the war, the Pandavas sought Shiva to atone. He hid from them as a bull in a herd. Bhima spotted him, and the bull dove into the earth. Bhima caught only the hump, and it stays at Kedarnath. The other parts rose at the Panch Kedar.

*He can be found, but not held.*

title: Nataraja
subtitle: नटराज · lord of the dance
body_markdown:
In Chidambaram, Shiva danced the universe into being and out of it, inside a ring of fire. The drum creates, the raised hand protects, the flame dissolves, the planted foot conceals and the lifted foot frees.

*The last bead, and the first motion. Then you turn the mala and begin again.*
